title: Conservation Cannon: Fox, Duck & the Coffee Mat Launcher
description: A Fox and a Duck sit on opposite ends of a coffee mat balanced on a fulcrum, forming a seesaw-launcher system. The user adjusts mass, spring tension, drop height, and launch angle to fire the Duck into a target zone while conserving momentum and energy. Undo/redo buttons let the user revert any parameter change, and a real-time energy bar tracks kinetic, potential, and elastic energy conservation throughout each launch.
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a physics seesaw-launcher. Load Fox.glb, Duck.glb, and coffeemat.glb via GLTFLoader. Place the coffeemat flat as the seesaw plank, centered on a visible triangular fulcrum prism at world origin. Position the Duck on the left end of the mat and the Fox hovering above the right end at an adjustable drop height. Camera: perspective at (0,5,12) looking at origin. Lighting: hemisphere light plus directional light with shadows enabled on a ground plane.

Interaction steps (10-14 total): (1) Slider to set Fox mass (1-5 kg). (2) Slider to set Duck mass (0.5-3 kg). (3) Slider to set Fox drop height (1-5 m). (4) Slider to set fulcrum offset along the mat (-1 to 1 normalized). (5) Slider to set launch angle modifier (0-45 degrees added tilt). (6) Toggle a hidden spring under the Duck end with adjustable spring constant slider (50-500 N/m). (7) Click 'Drop Fox' button — Fox falls under gravity, hits mat right side, mat rotates around fulcrum, transferring momentum to Duck. (8) Duck launches into the air following projectile motion computed from conservation of energy and momentum. (9) Display real-time energy bar (KE, PE, elastic) showing total energy is conserved within 2%. (10) A translucent target ring floats at a computed ideal landing spot; score based on how close Duck lands. (11-12) Undo and Redo buttons revert/reapply any slider or parameter change, maintaining a history stack of at least 10 states. (13) Reset button restores all defaults and repositions models. (14) After landing, show a results panel with launch velocity, max height, range, and energy conservation percentage.

Animate Fox falling with gravity (9.81 m/s²), mat rotation with moment of inertia, and Duck parabolic flight. Use requestAnimationFrame loop. Fox should play its walk animation while idle and stop on impact. Duck bobs gently before launch. All UI controls in an overlay div with clean styling.
